summary: The enterprise AI model API landscape in 2026 is dominated by the three hyperscalers—AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI/Foundry, and Google Vertex AI—each offering managed, secure access to dozens of foundation models without data leaving the customer's cloud boundary. A strong second tier includes data-platform-native players (Snowflake Cortex AI), hybrid/governance-focused vendors (IBM watsonx), edge-inference providers (Cloudflare Workers AI), and Oracle Cloud AI for existing OCI shops. There is no single winner—selection depends on existing cloud contracts, data gravity, compliance needs, and the specific models required.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: prompts and completions stay inside the company's own cloud tenancy/VPC rather than being sent to a third-party vendor's public API, satisfying data-sovereignty requirements.

Compliance and certifications: aggregators inherit the cloud provider's SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR and regional residency controls, drastically reducing audit burden versus going direct to a model vendor.
Single billing and existing cloud commitments: usage draws down on committed cloud spend (EDP/MACC/enterprise agreements), consolidating procurement, invoicing, and vendor management.
Model choice and avoiding lock-in: one secure API gives access to many model families (Claude, Llama, Gemini, Mistral, GPT, etc.) so teams can swap or benchmark models without re-architecting.
Enterprise controls at scale: built-in VPC/private networking, IAM, audit logging, guardrails/content filtering, fine-tuning, and provisioned throughput that raw vendor APIs often lack.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service (Microsoft Foundry)
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K/1M tokens (input/output priced separately); Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved, predictable capacity; batch pricing discounts.
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-centric enterprises wanting first-and-exclusive access to OpenAI frontier models with deep M365/Azure integration.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-token pricing; Provisioned Throughput (model units) for reserved capacity; batch inference discounts; Marketplace models with vendor pricing.
platforms.best_for: AWS-native enterprises wanting the broadest multi-vendor model choice (especially Claude) with strong agent and RAG tooling.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token / per-character and per-image; Provisioned Throughput sold in GSUs (Generative AI Scale Units) — e.g. 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash ≈ 67,250 tokens/sec sustained; committed use discounts.
key_features: Grounding with Google Search & RAG Engine
platforms.best_for: Data/analytics-heavy and Google-ecosystem enterprises wanting Gemini plus a large multimodal model garden and strong MLOps.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits by model and token usage; no separate model contracts.
key_features: Models run inside Snowflake governance perimeter (data never leaves)
platforms.best_for: Enterprises with data gravity in Snowflake wanting to run LLMs directly against governed warehouse data without data movement.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Subscription plus Resource Unit (RU) token-based consumption; SaaS, hybrid, and on-prem (Cloud Pak for Data) licensing options.
platforms.best_for: Regulated industries and hybrid/on-prem enterprises prioritizing AI governance, auditability, and IBM ecosystem integration. Named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for AI Platforms.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Serverless pay-per-use billed in 'Neurons' (compute units) with a free allocation; no infrastructure to manage.
key_features: AI Gateway for caching, rate limiting, logging & analytics
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency, globally distributed inference on open models at the edge, often as a gateway in front of other providers.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Per-character / per-token on-demand; dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity and fine-tuning; committed cloud spend eligible.
platforms.best_for: Oracle database and ERP/Fusion customers wanting generative AI close to Oracle workloads, and sovereignty-sensitive deployments.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI (Foundation Model APIs)
platforms.pricing: Consumption via Databricks Units (DBUs); pay-per-token foundation model APIs plus provisioned throughput for dedicated endpoints.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises with a lakehouse data strategy wanting to build, govern, and serve custom and foundation models alongside their data and ML pipelines.
